boundary_rationale: This unit opens the book with the title-and-provenance formula, דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן חִלְקִיָּ֑הוּ מִן הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֔וֹת בְּאֶ֖רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן (oshb:Jer.1.1, byte tier), rendered “The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin” (web:Jer.1.1). The heading then dates the prophet’s word-ministry across a three-reign span — Josiah’s thirteenth year (web:Jer.1.2) through the eleventh year of Zedekiah and Jerusalem’s captivity in the fifth month (web:Jer.1.3) — before any narrative word-event formula appears; the vayehi devar-YHWH onset that opens the call narrative sits at Jer.1.4 (oshb:Jer.1.4), outside this span, so this unit stops at the heading’s own close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the call narrative was considered and rejected: the dated title-and-provenance heading and the narrative vayehi devar-YHWH formula belong to structurally distinct device classes.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah closes the Masoretic parashah layer at Jer.1.3 (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets' weak-tier reading, not a boundary driver by itself). The heading names both Jeremiah's priestly father, Hilkiah, and his home town, Anathoth in Benjamin, before any reported divine speech begins.

boundary_rationale: A fresh scene opens with the narrative word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.1.4, byte tier) — “Now Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.1.4) — the first of the vayehi devar-YHWH onsets that structure the book’s frame spine. The dialogue that follows (the appointment as a prophet, the touched mouth, the commissioning “Behold, I have today set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant” (web:Jer.1.10)) stays inside one unit with its opening formula, since the speaker and addressee do not change across the exchange; a fresh word-event onset instead marks the boundary at Jer.1.11 (oshb:Jer.1.11), where the next vision report opens.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at Jeremiah's protest in web:Jer.1.6 (“Ah, Lord Yahweh”) was considered and rejected, since the protest and Yahweh's answer are turns inside the same call dialogue rather than a fresh scene or addressee.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah at Jer.1.3 (single-witness, tier-3) closes the heading just before this span opens; interior petuchah breaks fall after Jer.1.6 and after Jer.1.10 (single-witness, tier-3), the latter aligning with this unit’s own close. Jeremiah’s protest carries the title stack אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.1.6, byte tier; adonai YHWH). The reassurance “to rescue you” (web:Jer.1.8) recurs in close wording at the charge’s own close (web:Jer.1.19), a rescue-formula bracket around the call and both vision reports that follow it, even though this unit and the vision reports are kept as separate rows here.

boundary_rationale: A second word-event formula opens a vision report: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר מָה אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וָאֹמַ֕ר מַקֵּ֥ל שָׁקֵ֖ד אֲנִ֥י רֹאֶֽה (oshb:Jer.1.11, byte tier) — Moreover Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” I said, “I see a branch of an almond tree.” (web:Jer.1.11). Yahweh’s reply plays on the answer’s sound: כִּֽי שֹׁקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.12, byte tier) — Then Yahweh said to me, “You have seen well; for I watch over my word to perform it.” (web:Jer.1.12) — pairing shaqed (almond) with shoqed (watching). The unit closes with that wordplay; a third word-event formula, explicitly marked as recurring a second time, opens the next vision at Jer.1.13 (oshb:Jer.1.13).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this vision into the call narrative that precedes it was considered and rejected, since its own word-event formula (oshb:Jer.1.11) reopens the frame spine rather than continuing web:Jer.1.10's commission without a break.
literature_type_guess: call-vision report built on a sound pun
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Petuchah breaks bracket this short unit at both ends, after Jer.1.10 and after Jer.1.12 (single-witness, tier-3), matching its span exactly. The almond/watching pun is lexically distinct from the sheqer (falsehood) keyword that recurs later in the book; a bare two-letter sweep would blend the pair, so the pun is named by its own root here rather than counted against sheqer.

boundary_rationale: The formula recurs with an explicit ordinal marker: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר סִ֤יר נָפ֨וּחַ֙ אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֔ה וּפָנָ֖יו מִפְּנֵ֥י צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier) — Yahweh’s word came to me the second time, saying, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a boiling cauldron; and it is tipping away from the north.” (web:Jer.1.13). The interpretation that follows (web:Jer.1.14-16, disaster breaking from the north, kingdoms setting their thrones at Jerusalem’s gates) stays with its vision report under one frame, since no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides them; it adds neither a formula nor a new imperative or addressee of its own. A direct second-person charge to the prophet, marked by an imperative construction, opens the next unit at Jer.1.17 (oshb:Jer.1.17).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between the vision proper (web:Jer.1.13) and its interpretation (web:Jer.1.14-16) was considered and rejected: the interpretation introduces neither a formula, an imperative, nor a fresh addressee of its own, so it reads as the same speech continuing rather than a fresh unit.
literature_type_guess: call-vision report with a northern-invader oracle
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A petuchah stands at Jer.1.12, immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory is silent inside 1:13-16 and at this unit's own close. The kingdoms-of-the-north motif introduced here (web:Jer.1.15) recurs across the book's foe-from-the-north material; this unit is where it is introduced, ahead of the tsafon material spread through the rest of this span.

boundary_rationale: A direct charge to the prophet opens with an imperative construction: וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier) — “You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise” (web:Jer.1.17) — turning from the vision report’s content back to second-person address of Jeremiah himself, echoing the don’t-be-afraid charge of web:Jer.1.8. The unit closes with אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier) — “to rescue you.” (web:Jer.1.19) — the same rescue clause that closed web:Jer.1.8, bracketing the call narrative and both vision reports that precede it. Chapter 1 ends here; a fresh word-event formula opens the next unit at Jer.2.1 (oshb:Jer.2.1).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.1.17-19 as the closing three verses of the second vision report rather than its own unit was considered: unlike Jer.1.13's own onset, the imperative here carries no word-event formula, so the case for a fresh unit rests on the addressee shift and the rescue-clause bracket with web:Jer.1.8 rather than on formula repetition.
literature_type_guess: commissioning charge with a rescue-formula bracket
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A petuchah closes this unit and chapter 1 together at Jer.1.19 (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory is silent through the rest of the span. The fortified-city and iron-pillar imagery of web:Jer.1.18 belongs to the same charge as the gird-your-loins imperative that opens it, so it is carried inside this unit rather than treated as a fresh onset.

boundary_rationale: Chapter 2 opens with its own word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.2.1, byte tier) — “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.2.1) — immediately followed by a go-and-proclaim imperative introducing quoted divine speech: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) — “the kindness of your youth, your love as a bride” (web:Jer.2.2). The oracle recalls Israel’s early devotion and closes with a threat against those who devour her, marked by the closing formula in web:Jer.2.3. A fresh discourse-frame imperative addressed to the house of Jacob opens the next unit at Jer.2.4 (oshb:Jer.2.4).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A salvation_oracle label was considered for this span, given the positive covenant memory in web:Jer.2.2, and rejected in favor of judgment_oracle: the unit's own close threatens harm on those who wrong Israel and the material functions as the forensic prologue to the indictment that follows rather than a future-restoration promise.
literature_type_guess: covenant-memory oracle framed by a go-proclaim command

device_notes: A petuchah stands at Jer.1.19, immediately before this span (single-witness, tier-3, disclosed here for symmetry with the preceding unit's own close); a second petuchah closes this unit's own span at Jer.2.3. The bridal-love and wilderness-devotion imagery is bounded by its own go-and-proclaim frame rather than left as free-standing lyric.

boundary_rationale: An attend-the-word imperative addressed to the whole house of Israel opens the covenant lawsuit proper: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) — “Hear Yahweh’s word, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel!” (web:Jer.2.4). The unit runs the formal rib pattern through to its evidentiary close: the fathers’ baseless complaint (web:Jer.2.5), the wilderness rehearsal (web:Jer.2.6-7), the priests’/prophets’ failure (web:Jer.2.8), the verdict announcement at web:Jer.2.9, the coastland witnesses (web:Jer.2.10), the astonished-heavens summons (web:Jer.2.12), and the twin-evil indictment closing at web:Jer.2.13. No fresh imperative or formula intervenes before Jer.2.14, where a rhetorical-question series shifts the argument’s shape.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the rhetorical questions of web:Jer.2.14ff was considered and rejected: those verses lack a witness summons or verdict language of the rib pattern's own kind, so the formal lawsuit is read as closing at its own evidentiary close in web:Jer.2.13.

device_notes: A petuchah at Jer.2.3 falls immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory is silent inside 2:4-13 and at its close. The heavens-and-coastlands witness summons (web:Jer.2.10, web:Jer.2.12) is the classic covenant-lawsuit evidentiary device, distinguishing this unit's formal legal shape from the looser indictment discourse that follows it.

boundary_rationale: The argument shifts from formal lawsuit to a sustained run of rhetorical questions: הַעֶ֨בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָבַֽז (oshb:Jer.2.14, byte tier) — “Is Israel a slave? Is he born into slavery? Why has he become a captive?” (web:Jer.2.14). Nothing in this span carries a fresh word-event formula, koh-amar onset, discourse imperative, or addressee shift as the indictment moves through the vine (web:Jer.2.21), dromedary and donkey (web:Jer.2.23-24), and idol-futility (web:Jer.2.27-28) metaphors; the unit is held together as one span rather than cut at those metaphor changes, which mark topic, not formula. It closes “Your own sword has devoured your prophets” (web:Jer.2.30); an attend-the-word imperative opens the next unit at Jer.2.31 (oshb:Jer.2.31).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting this span at the vine, dromedary-and-donkey, and idol-futility metaphor changes (web:Jer.2.21, web:Jer.2.23, web:Jer.2.27) was considered and rejected for lacking a formula, imperative, or addressee-shift warrant of the kind that bounds the units on either side of it; those shifts are content transitions inside one sustained divine indictment, held here at medium confidence given the length this span reaches without such a warrant appearing inside it.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah falls at Jer.2.28, inside this span (single-witness, tier-3); no formula or imperative accompanies it, so it is disclosed as texture rather than adopted as an internal boundary. The title stack ‘adonai YHWH (tsevaot)’ closes two sub-movements inside this unit, at web:Jer.2.19 and web:Jer.2.22, without a fresh addressee following either time.

boundary_rationale: A vocative attend-the-word imperative reopens the indictment: הַדּ֗וֹר אַתֶּם֙ רְא֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה הֲמִדְבָּ֤ר הָיִ֨יתִי֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֛ם אֶ֥רֶץ מַאְפֵּ֖לְיָ֑ה מַדּ֜וּעַ אָמְר֤וּ עַמִּי֙ רַ֔דְנוּ לֽוֹא נָב֥וֹא ע֖וֹד אֵלֶֽיךָ (oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier) — “Generation, consider Yahweh’s word. Have I been a wilderness to Israel? Or a land of thick darkness? Why do my people say, ‘We have broken loose. We will come to you no more’?” (web:Jer.2.31), pairing a ‘see’ imperative with ‘Yahweh’s word’ as its object, the same discourse-frame shape as the ‘hear’ imperative of web:Jer.2.4. The unit runs through the virgin-and-ornaments figure (web:Jer.2.32), the seeking-love charge (web:Jer.2.33), and the innocent-blood accusation (web:Jer.2.34) to the chapter’s own close in web:Jer.2.37, where the marks and formula inventories carry nothing further before Jer.3.1’s topic shift. This unit’s own close relies on the chapter boundary together with that shift into the divorce-law analogy, rather than on a formula of its own, so it is held at reduced confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Jer.2.31 as a continuation of the preceding indictment rather than a fresh unit was considered and rejected, since its vocative opening repeats the attend-the-word imperative shape of web:Jer.2.4 closely enough to argue for a renewed onset rather than silent continuation.
literature_type_guess: indictment discourse reopened by an attend-the-word imperative

device_notes: No parashah mark falls at this unit's front seam, inside its span, or at its own close; the marks inventory is silent across 2:30-2:37, an absence that is not read as counterevidence against the boundaries argued here from the imperative and the chapter close alone.

boundary_rationale: A case-law analogy opens the chapter without a formula of its own: “They say, ‘If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him, and becomes another man’s, should he return to her again?” (web:Jer.3.1). The analogy turns to direct application at the same verse’s close: וְאַ֗תְּ זָנִית֙ רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וְשׁ֥וֹב אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier) — “But you have played the prostitute with many lovers; yet return again to me” (web:Jer.3.1) — the earliest skeleton-tier occurrence of the shuv (return) root book-wide (sweep: 41 verses, skeleton tier, earliest at Jer.3.1). The address continues through the bare-heights imagery (web:Jer.3.2) and the withheld-rain consequence (web:Jer.3.3) to a quoted plea at web:Jer.3.4-5. This unit’s onset rests on the analogy’s topic shift rather than a formula or imperative, so it is held at reduced confidence; a fresh scene, marked by a dated speech-introduction, opens the next unit at Jer.3.6 (oshb:Jer.3.6).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Jer.3.1 as a direct continuation of web:Jer.2.31-37 without a fresh unit was considered: the divorce-law case introduces a new controlling legal analogy not present in the preceding material, which argues for a fresh onset even though no word-event or koh-amar formula marks the transition.
literature_type_guess: case-law analogy applied to covenant unfaithfulness

device_notes: A petuchah closes this unit's own span at Jer.3.5 (single-witness, tier-3); the marks inventory carries nothing inside 3:1-4 or at the front seam. The seam onset at web:Jer.3.1 opens the shuv-wordplay cluster that runs to the close of this span at Jer.4.4; its internal divisions in this and the following three units are cut where the bytes themselves carry a warrant, per this book's held posture on the cluster's edges.

boundary_rationale: A dated scene-introduction reopens direct address to the prophet: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.3.6, byte tier) — “Yahweh said to me in the days of Josiah the king” (web:Jer.3.6), asking, “Have you seen that which backsliding Israel has done?” (web:Jer.3.6) — pairing a fresh speech-introduction verb with an explicit reign anchor, distinct from the vayehi devar-YHWH shape used at this book’s earlier word-event onsets. The retrospective on Israel and “her treacherous sister” Judah (web:Jer.3.7-9) closes “but only in pretense” (web:Jer.3.10). The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a fresh statement at Jer.3.11 (oshb:Jer.3.11), marking this unit’s own close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the 'Yahweh said to me' introductions at web:Jer.3.6 and web:Jer.3.11 as one shared introduction covering both verses' material was considered and rejected: the verb recurs in full rather than carrying over, and the register shifts between the two sites, from past-tense retrospective (3:6-10) to a present comparison and a go-proclaim command (3:11ff).

device_notes: Petuchah breaks bracket this unit at both ends, after Jer.3.5 and after Jer.3.10 (single-witness, tier-3), matching its span exactly. The meshuvah (backsliding) noun that names Israel across this book's wordplay cluster appears twice here, at web:Jer.3.6 and web:Jer.3.8.

boundary_rationale: The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a comparative statement, then pivots into command: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) — “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah” (web:Jer.3.11), continuing directly into הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier) — “Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Yahweh; ‘I will not look in anger on you, for I am merciful,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will not keep anger forever” (web:Jer.3.12) — a go-and-proclaim imperative carrying the shuv invitation. The promised restoration (shepherds, the ark forgotten, Jerusalem as Yahweh’s throne, Judah and Israel reunited: web:Jer.3.15-18) and Yahweh’s own reflection on disappointed hope (web:Jer.3.19-20) continue inside the same continuing speech, since no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee divides them from the invitation that opens it. A narrated scene shift — a voice heard weeping, rather than reported divine speech — opens the next unit at Jer.3.21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at the emphatic pivot opening web:Jer.3.19 was considered, since the WEB rendering opens a fresh quotation there; it was rejected for lacking a word-event formula, koh-amar onset, or imperative of the kind that bounds this book's other seams, so the reflection is kept inside the larger invitation-and-promise unit at reduced confidence rather than split on that softer signal alone.

boundary_rationale: A narrated scene, not reported divine speech, opens this unit: ק֚וֹל עַל שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier) — “A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Israel; because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God” (web:Jer.3.21) — shifting from the first-person divine promise of the preceding unit to third-person description of a sound. Yahweh’s renewed call, שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) — “Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding” (web:Jer.3.22) — is answered inside the same unit by the community’s own first-person-plural confession, “Behold, we have come to you” (web:Jer.3.22) through “we have sinned against Yahweh our God” (web:Jer.3.25), closing “We have not obeyed Yahweh our God’s voice” (web:Jer.3.25). A conditional address to ‘Israel’ by name, resuming Yahweh’s own voice, opens the next unit at Jer.4.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.3.22's imperative opening as the true onset, with web:Jer.3.21 held back as the close of the preceding restoration promise, was considered and rejected: the voice-heard-weeping scene lacks an addressee or formula tying it to the prior unit's promise, and it motivates the call and confession that follow it rather than concluding what precedes it.
literature_type_guess: penitential lament scene with communal confession

boundary_rationale: Yahweh’s own voice resumes, addressing ‘Israel’ by name in a conditional construction: אִם תָּשׁ֨וּב יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל נְאֻם יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י תָּשׁ֑וּב וְאִם תָּסִ֧יר שִׁקּוּצֶ֛יךָ מִפָּנַ֖י וְלֹ֥א תָנֽוּד (oshb:Jer.4.1, byte tier) — “If you will return, Israel,” (web:Jer.4.1) — turning from the community’s own confessional voice back to a divine speech-turn. The oath-and-blessing consequence in web:Jer.4.2 closes this short unit before a koh-amar onset, addressed by name to the men of Judah and Jerusalem rather than to Israel, opens the next unit at Jer.4.3 (oshb:Jer.4.3).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding web:Jer.4.1-2 into the confession scene that precedes it was considered and rejected: the speaking voice returns to Yahweh's own conditional address, and the addressee narrows explicitly to 'Israel' by name rather than continuing the community's first-person-plural confession.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah falls at Jer.3.25, immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3, disclosed here for symmetry with the preceding unit's own close); a second setumah closes this unit's own span at Jer.4.2. The shuv root recurs here, continuing since web:Jer.3.1, in both halves of web:Jer.4.1's conditional.

boundary_rationale: A koh-amar onset addressed to a newly named audience opens this unit: כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְאַֽל תִּזְרְע֖וּ אֶל קוֹצִֽים (oshb:Jer.4.3, byte tier) — rendered “For Yahweh says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem”, with the command following, “Break up your fallow ground, and don’t sow among thorns” (web:Jer.4.3) — the frame-owner is Yahweh, and the addressee narrows explicitly from ‘Israel’ (web:Jer.4.1) to the men of Judah and Jerusalem, a combined koh-amar onset and addressee shift. The circumcise-your-heart imperative of web:Jer.4.4 closes this unit and this span together; a discourse-frame imperative (‘declare and blow the trumpet’) follows beyond this span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.4.3-4 as a continuation of the conditional oracle in web:Jer.4.1-2 was considered and rejected: the koh-amar frame-owner formula and the explicit narrowing of the addressee to the men of Judah and Jerusalem mark a fresh onset rather than a continuation of the address to 'Israel'.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah at Jer.4.2 falls immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3, disclosed here for symmetry with the preceding unit's own close); the marks inventory is silent from there through this unit's own close at Jer.4.4, an absence not read as counterevidence. The heart-circumcision figure of web:Jer.4.4 closes both this unit and this span at the same verse.
